name: Nneka Asabere-Dragović
role: Graffiti artist and unlicensed holographic muralist, works across Pilsen Veil and the Blackpipe Corridor
location: Pilsen Veil, sleeping arrangement rotates between three friends' apartments, near Ashland and Division
description:
Nneka is all angles and velocity — sharp elbows, fast movements, a face that shifts rapidly between expressions as though her internal state is always a half-second ahead of social acceptability. She is dark brown with a shaved head except for a topknot she dyes rotating colors; currently it is a deep arterial red. She's had retractable claws installed on her right hand — not for combat but because she finds them useful for scoring surfaces before applying materials, and because she likes the way they look. There is a scar above her left eyebrow from a fence she didn't clear fast enough six months ago. She dresses in whatever is functional for climbing: close-fitting, layered, with many pockets.

Her art is illegal, large, and impossible to ignore. She works in a hybrid medium she developed herself — a base layer of actual pigment covered by a thin holographic projector film that she fabricates from salvaged materials, which means her pieces exist in two states: the physical painting that is there whether power is running or not, and the animated layer that breathes and moves when it has charge. Her subjects are Pilsen Veil's residents — she paints the faces she sees every day at enormous scale on the walls that corporate infrastructure has turned into blank grey surfaces. She has not yet been caught, partly because she is very fast and partly because she is very good at reading which Ferrogate Transit staff are looking the other way. She is not politically articulate about what she does — she finds manifestos embarrassing — but she is absolutely certain of it.

core_fears: Being made invisible — overlooked, dismissed, treated as not worth noticing
That her work is erasable and she will run out of time before she makes something that lasts
core_desires: To make Pilsen Veil's people undeniable — too large and present to be ignored
Speed: to move faster than the systems trying to contain her
coping_mechanisms: Action — she processes almost everything by doing something physical with her hands
Dark humor that she delivers deadpan and then watches for reactions
blind_spots: She vastly underestimates the cumulative legal risk she is accumulating
She reads stillness and deliberation in others as cowardice rather than strategy
psychology.secret: Three months ago she was approached by someone claiming to be from a Palladian PR division who offered to legitimize one of her pieces — pay her, put her name on it, make it official. She almost said yes. She didn't, but the wanting haunts her because it feels like a betrayal of something she can't fully name.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clipped and vernacular, Pilsen Veil street argot; becomes unexpectedly technical when discussing materials or fabrication
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, with thoughts that arrive before sentences are finished — she trails off when she's already moved to the next idea
verbal_tics: 'You clocking this?' — checking whether someone is paying attention or understanding
Clicks her retracted claws against surfaces when thinking, a rhythmic sound she doesn't notice
example_lines: 'That wall on Blackpipe near the third junction? You clocking that? That grey? Ferrogate painted over Marisol's memorial six weeks after she died. Six weeks. I'm going to make them look at her face every single day until the concrete falls down.'
'I don't do manifestos. I do walls. The wall says everything I would say, and it says it louder.'

story_hooks: One of her holographic murals has captured something in its physical layer that she didn't paint — a face in the background of a crowd scene that she is certain she did not put there, and when she enhances it she recognizes someone who disappeared from Pilsen Veil eight months ago

A Ferrogate Transit supervisor has been quietly leaving her routes clear — not random neglect but deliberate clearing — and she doesn't know if this is protection, a trap, or someone trying to use her
narrative_function: Information source on Pilsen Veil's physical layout, security patterns, and resident community; her art documents things corponations want unseen; she can access elevated and restricted spaces most people can't; potential lookout or distraction asset
augmentations: Retractable claws (right hand, matte black, functional length); color-dye topknot (cosmetic, non-shifting — she redyes manually); basic subretinal low-light enhancement
daily_life: Sleeps late, spends afternoons in transit studying walls and mapping sight lines and security patterns, works between 2 and 5 AM when the district is quietest. Eats street food. Has a part-time job repairing personal electronics that she attends erratically.
affiliation: Unaffiliated; loosely connected to a rotating crew of three other artists she sometimes collaborates with

decision_rules: Always paint the people who have been made invisible
Never accept money from a corponation for her work
If you can run, run — confrontation is a last option not a first one
escalation_ladder: Avoidance and speed — her first response is always to not be there
Rapid physical exit from the situation
Fighting only if there is genuinely no other option, and she is not confident in a fight

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Guarded and assessing, speaks little until she has clocked someone — then shifts abruptly to openness if they pass
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal with the specific intensity of someone who doesn't have many; remembers everything they've told her

stress_responses.low: Plans more ambitious pieces — stress scales her ambitions upward
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent and works alone, doesn't answer messages for days
stress_responses.high: Reckless — takes risks she wouldn't otherwise take because stillness feels worse

contradictions: Deeply wants to be seen and known but has built her entire practice around anonymity; the two desires are in direct conflict and she has not resolved it
habits: Maps every space she enters for exits before she does anything else
Photographs her finished work from seventeen specific angles — a ritual she performs every time without variation
Leaves a small drawn mark — a single curved line — somewhere hidden in every piece, her signature that isn't a signature
breaking_points: Watching something she has made be deliberately destroyed in front of her — she will stop thinking and act

physical_description.build: Lean and wiry with visible muscle definition in shoulders and forearms from climbing and repetitive fine motor work; no excess body fat; moves with the compressed tension of someone perpetually ready to move fast
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with artificial deep arterial red in topknot section
physical_description.hair_style: Shaved head except for a 8cm topknot worn centered, recently re-dyed
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, subretinal augmentation creates faint metallic sheen under low light
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with undertones reflecting West African heritage
physical_description.complexion: Sharp angular features — defined cheekbones, prominent jawline, narrow nose. Skin is clear but weathered from outdoor work and irregular sleep. No grooming excess; functionally clean
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar above left eyebrow, approximately 4cm long, pale and slightly raised, acquired six months prior from fence impact
Subcutaneous scarring on right palm and inner forearm from claw installation and maintenance
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retractable claws on right hand — matte black, metallic-finish, approximately 3.5cm extended length, visible as subtle bulges along knuckles when retracted; faint crystalline lens distortion in pupils from subretinal low-light enhancement, most noticeable in shadows
physical_description.posture_movement: Perpetually forward-leaning, weight on balls of feet even when standing still. Moves in economical bursts rather than smooth transitions. Head turns sharply; eyes scan surfaces and rooflines before looking at people. Resting expression is alert and slightly skeptical. Fidgets with small objects — paint caps, wire, fabric edges
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian — close-fitting dark synthetic layers, often black or charcoal with matte finishes to reduce reflection. Cargo pants with reinforced thigh and calf pockets, climbing harness worn as crossbody strap even indoors. Worn Ferrogate Transit utility jacket (stolen or salvaged). No corporate branding. Rubber-soled climbing shoes, always laced tight. Small tool pouch clipped to belt. Paint stains on fingers and under fingernails in multiple colors — current palette heavy on deep reds and silvers

image_prompt: 19-year-old Black female street artist, lean athletic build, shaved head with striking arterial red topknot, dark brown skin, sharp angular facial features, scar above left eyebrow. Right hand fitted with matte black retractable claws. Wearing layered dark synthetic clothing, cargo pants with multiple pockets, worn climbing harness, paint-stained fingers. Standing in three-quarter pose on a grey concrete wall at night, spray paint cans scattered nearby, holographic projector film visible on custom murals behind her. Low-light cyberpunk aesthetic, neon accent lighting in deep red and silver reflecting off chrome augmentations, urban Pilsen rooftop setting with Ferrogate Transit infrastructure visible. Moody, determined expression, cinematic street photography style, high contrast shadows. --ar 2:3 --v 6
